solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With most of the drink knocked back, it's time to sleep

indicators.note: knocked back says the assembled letters are turned round and read backwards
most of says the word that follows loses its final letter

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone downs most of their drink in one gulp and declares it bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses TH (most of 'the') plus GIN, giving the letters in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are the usual period for sleeping, so this phrase describes it.

clue.text: Peers etc showing no skill, lacking capital

indicators.note: lacking capital says the following word loses its first letter, its capital

parts.note: skill is ability

explanation.surface: A dig at the House of Lords: aristocrats with no talent at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking capital' suggests poverty but means dropping the first letter of ABILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers, dukes, earls and the like collectively form the aristocratic class.

clue.text: Woman showing some regret, always

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman who is forever showing a touch of remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Buy some insurance and hide

definitions.meaning: to obtain a policy protecting against loss is to get cover
to conceal oneself, shelter from fire or danger

explanation.surface: A cautious person both insures themselves and goes into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrase: buying protection under a policy, and sheltering out of sight.

clue.text: Professional with education degree asked searching questions

parts.note: pro is short for professional
BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A qualified teacher interrogating someone closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate thoroughly by close questioning is to delve, past tense here.

clue.text: Friend regularly supplied claret, perhaps

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the word Friend is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A pal who keeps you topped up with Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is an example of a wine of this colour, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Labour set up many elections

indicators.note: in a down clue set up says the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party
lots means many

explanation.surface: The Labour Party arranging lots of polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses LAB (Labour, the UK party) into BAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes cast in secret are the means of deciding polls, so they stand for elections.

clue.text: Small amount of alcohol doctor takes in the morning

parts.note: a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A physician with a morning tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, especially whisky.

clue.text: Back south of Croatian resort for a very short time

indicators.note: in a down clue south of puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: Split is a resort on the Croatian coast
to back a proposal is to second it

explanation.surface: Supporting a trip to Croatia briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as a noun but is the verb meaning support; in a down clue 'south of' places it lower in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an instant, a fraction of a moment.

clue.text: Become upset to finish school

definitions.meaning: to lose emotional control, start crying
when school ends for the holidays the pupils are said to do this

explanation.surface: A child getting emotional on the last day of term.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage schools 'break up' for the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrasal verb covers both collapsing emotionally and ending term.

clue.text: Speaker's given out a letter from Athens

indicators.note: speaker's says what follows is heard, a word that sounds like it

parts.note: given out means dealt, plus a

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a letter sent from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given out a' is DEALT A, which said quickly matches the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fourth character of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens.

clue.text: Empty lodge next to a field

indicators.note: empty says the word lodge has its insides removed, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: A deserted hunting lodge beside a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a meadow or pasture.

clue.text: Fried potatoes fresh from the pan? A hit at Troon

parts.note: chips are fried potato strips
just cooked food is hot

explanation.surface: Chips just out of the fryer.
explanation.walkthrough: Troon is a Scottish golf course that hosts the Open; the definition hides on the end of a food clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A short lofted golf stroke onto the green, the kind played at a links course.

clue.text: Uncle Rod's turned out to be a villain

indicators.note: turned out says the letters of these words are reorganised

explanation.surface: Family revelation: Uncle Rod was a crook all along.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal, a synonym for a wicked person.

clue.text: To begin with, some townspeople really annoy newcomer

indicators.note: to begin with says the opening letter of each of the next words is taken

parts.note: to anger is to annoy

explanation.surface: A new arrival who irritates the locals from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfamiliar who has just arrived in a place.

clue.text: Various novelties I prepared for the box

indicators.note: various says the letters of the following words are mixed up

parts.note: set means prepared, ready

explanation.surface: Someone getting assorted gadgets ready to pack in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the appliance in the living room that shows programmes.

clue.text: Go miles, wandering in French city

indicators.note: wandering says the letters of these words stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker covering great distances around a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in central France famous for porcelain.

clue.text: A fellow going round Morecambe maybe is from the States

indicators.note: going round says the second piece is enclosed by the first

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, so Eric is one Morecambe

explanation.surface: A man touring the seaside town of Morecambe turns out to be a Yank.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort; it is the comedian Eric Morecambe, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from the United States is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Male failing to finish cuppa

indicators.note: failing to finish says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A man who cannot drink his whole cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British informal words for a cup of tea.

clue.text: Head cook brings in sushi at last

indicators.note: brings in says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: at last says the final letter of sushi is taken

explanation.surface: A head chef finally adding sushi to the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader or principal person, synonym of the boss.

clue.text: Very little pressure to turn on the waterworks

parts.note: wee is Scottish for very small
p is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A plumber needing only slight pressure to start the water flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to start the tears is to cry.

clue.text: Musician's regal composition

indicators.note: composition says the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A musician's stately piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like a musical work but signals the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer, an example of a musician.

clue.text: Southern English town supplying grain for whiskey

definitions.meaning: a small town in East Sussex, on England's south coast
the cereal used to distil a type of American whiskey

explanation.surface: A town in the south of England providing grain for distillers.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the Sussex town and the cereal grain.

clue.text: Old railwaymen celebrate what carer's doing?

definitions.note: a phrase for an activity, matching the verb form

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, now defunct
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Retired railway workers rejoicing, and a question about a care worker's job.
explanation.walkthrough: NUR, the former National Union of Railwaymen, is a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending the sick is the activity of someone who looks after patients.

clue.text: Saintly disciple traps small bug

indicators.note: traps says the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: St Peter was one of the twelve disciples
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: St Peter catching a tiny insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy or badger them, a synonym.

clue.text: Prisoner seen backsliding in feature film

indicators.note: backsliding says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A convict spotted relapsing in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Prisoner seen' as the definition, but 'seen' is a link and 'in' is the indicator that the letters are inside 'feature film'.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict serving a life sentence.
